title: Typed output preservation shim: OpenAI Chat Completions -> Redwood streaming & function-call mapping
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a small compatibility shim that maps incoming OpenAI Chat Completions (v1) requests and streaming responses to Redwood's canonical streaming + structured-output model while preserving typed function call semantics. This ticket covers request shape normalization, deterministic function-call encoding, streaming chunk alignment, idempotent replay for partial streams, and a compliance test-suite for parity with OpenAI behavior used by legacy clients.
acceptance_criteria: Requests using OpenAI chat schema (messages, temperature, max_tokens, functions) are accepted and mapped to Redwood's internal route without altering intent or function argument types

Streaming responses mirror token-by-token semantics: early tool-invocation signals, partial JSON chunks for structured outputs, and final completion event are reproducible compared to reference fixtures

Function calls in responses preserve name, argument types (strings, numbers, booleans, nested objects) and are emitted as a single coherent 'function_call' event under Redwood's structured output model
Idempotent resume: if a client reconnects mid-stream using the same session token, the shim can replay last confirmed frame and resume without duplicating side-effectful function calls
Automated compliance tests (fixtures for 20+ canonical scenarios) pass in CI; includes both streaming and non-streaming flows, tool failure, tool fallback and conflicting schema edge-cases
tasks: Draft mapping spec: request field equivalences and edge-case rules (Aisha)
Implement request normalizer: headers, role mapping, system/prefix handling (Marco)
Streaming frame translator: token framing, chunk reassembly, partial JSON buffering for structured output
Function-call encoder/decoder: preserve arg types and ensure single-event emission for function invocation
Build test harness: replayable stream recorder + fixture comparator
Add integration smoke tests against a mocked OpenAI CC endpoint and Redwood dev runtime
Performance benchmark: measure overhead introduced by shim at 50 RPS and validate <3% P99 latency regression
decisions: We will NOT attempt to canonicalize or coerce user-provided function schemas beyond preserving types; coercion creates surprising behavior for callers.
Use a lightweight in-memory buffer for partial JSON assembly with clear backpressure signals to the upstream runtime instead of heavy-weight transactional logs to minimize latency.
Expose an opt-in header X-Redwood-Compat=oa-chat for customers that want the OpenAI wire semantics; default behavior will be Redwood-first structured output mapping.
Function calls will be represented as Redwood structured 'tool_call' events in the same position as OpenAI's function_call object to ease consumption by legacy clients.
Idempotency key surface: accept OpenAI-like session_id or fallback to deterministic hash of request payload; documented in mapping spec.
notes: Design doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-example-design-doc - contains mapping tables and example payloads
Related infra ticket: ENG-412587 (streaming backpressure improvements) should land first to avoid head-of-line blocking
Coordination: PM (Lina Gomez) requested parity for function argument typing in order to support existing enterprise clients migrating to Redwood
Edge-case: OpenAI sometimes emits function_call with arguments as a single stringified JSON; we will attempt to parse when safe but preserve original string in fallback field 'raw_arguments'
